title: ScrollArea
summary: The standard SwiftUI ScrollView. The system draws the scroll indicators in every theme. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a panel, a log or a row of items that scrolls inside a screen. Set a height or a maximum height on it, and use scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize) so short content does not move.
whenNotToUse: For a whole screen of rows use List, which scrolls itself and reuses rows. Do not put a vertical ScrollView inside another vertical ScrollView.
api: func scrollIndicators(_ visibility: ScrollIndicatorVisibility, axes: Axis.Set = [.vertical, .horizontal]) -> some View
func scrollBounceBehavior(_ behavior: ScrollBounceBehavior, axes: Axis.Set = [.vertical]) -> some View

states.name: scrolling
states.description: The system indicator appears while the content moves and fades afterwards.

states.name: content fits
states.description: With scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize) the content does not bounce and no indicator is shown.

appearance: The indicators are drawn by the system and follow the light or dark appearance. The scroll view has no background; put it on a theme colour.
platformNotes: The web ScrollArea styles thin scrollbars to match the theme and makes the region focusable and labelled only when it scrolls. On iOS the indicators are the system's and cannot be themed, and a scroll view needs no focus stop: VoiceOver scrolls with three fingers and Full Keyboard Access scrolls the focused region. The web's height and maxHeight are frame(height:) and frame(maxHeight:). Not available: the web's edge shadows (shadows) and onScrollableChange; iOS 17 has no public signal for whether content overflows. Android uses its own scroll modifiers in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver scrolls with a three-finger swipe and announces the page.
System behaviour: moving VoiceOver or keyboard focus to an element outside the visible part scrolls it into view.
Add accessibilityLabel to the ScrollView only when the region needs a name of its own, for example a log.
edgeCases: A ScrollView takes all the height it is offered; without a frame it fills the screen.
scrollIndicators(.visible) is a request. The system still hides the indicator when the content fits.
A horizontal ScrollView inside a vertical one works; two on the same axis do not.
